snapshot_note: Snapshot as of 2026-09-30. Cells come from each tool's own docs/posts at the dates shown; not re-verified beyond that pass.

features.label: Runs more than one kind of agent
features.description: Can drive more than one coding agent (Claude Code, Codex and so on) side by side.

features.label: Coding agents supported
features.description: How many different coding agents it can run, per its own docs.

features.label: Alerts when you're needed
features.description: How it tells you an agent is waiting on you.

features.label: Answer "Allow?" prompts from the manager
features.description: When an agent stops to ask permission (run this command? edit this file?), you can allow or deny it from the manager or your phone instead of opening that agent's own window.

features.label: Hand-offs between agents in one view
features.description: Work passed from one agent to another shows up in the same place.

features.label: Always-on assistant
features.description: A standing assistant session you can reach any time.

features.label: Chat view of a session
features.description: Read a session as a conversation instead of raw terminal text.

features.label: Open the real terminal
features.description: Drop into the session's actual terminal.

features.label: How sessions are organized
features.description: List, worktrees, kanban or nested groups.

features.label: Prompt drafts
features.description: Draft prompts and insert them without sending.

features.label: Saved prompts
features.description: Reusable prompts you can fire with context attached.

features.label: Built-in editor / browser
features.description: Ships its own editor or browser.

features.label: Look and font control
features.description: How far you can change its look, including your terminal's font.

features.label: Shows your usage limits
features.description: Your subscription usage and resets, read from local logs.

features.label: Predicts when you'll hit a limit
features.description: Burn rate and time to the limit, not just current usage.

features.label: Pause and resume at usage limits
features.description: Pauses work near a limit and picks it back up after the reset.

features.label: Switch accounts without logging in again
features.description: Move between provider accounts without re-login.

features.label: Tasks from your notes vault
features.description: Reads your own notes vault (such as Obsidian) as the task list.

features.label: Turns GitHub or Jira issues into pull requests
features.description: Picks up an issue from GitHub, GitLab, Linear or Jira, hands it to an agent, and carries the resulting pull request through review.

features.label: Manages git worktrees
features.description: Gives each agent or task its own git worktree.

features.label: Planner that splits the work
features.description: Breaks a goal into parts and runs them.

features.label: Agents message each other
features.description: One session can message or query another.

features.label: Knowledge base for agents
features.description: A notes store agents can look things up in.

features.label: Phone app
features.description: A dedicated iOS or Android app.

features.label: Phone access with no new app
features.description: Reach it from your phone with tools you already have.

features.label: Remote machines over SSH
features.description: Run or edit sessions on another machine.

features.label: Voice input
features.description: Dictate to it.

features.label: Operating systems
features.description: Which systems it runs on, plus phone or browser access, per its own release files or docs.

features.label: App shell
features.description: What the app is built on: Electron, Tauri, a terminal UI, or a hosted service.

features.label: Main languages
features.description: Top languages in its repo, from GitHub's breakdown.

features.label: Background process
features.description: Whether it runs a separate server or daemon next to the app.

features.label: Download size
features.description: Installer size from its latest release. Not memory use.

features.label: Memory vs Claude Desktop
features.description: Size as a share of Claude Desktop, counting the app and the virtual machine it starts for Cowork. Scale: Tiny = under 5%, Small = 5-15%, Medium = 15-40%. Each tool's cell is an estimate from what the tool is built on. The coding agents themselves cost the same under every tool.

features.label: Runs in your own terminal
features.description: Lives inside the terminal you already use.

features.label: License / cost
features.description: Open-source license or pricing.

features.label: Plugins / SDK
features.description: Outside developers can extend it.

features.label: Teams
features.description: Built for more than one person.

features.label: Maturity
features.description: How far along and how stable it is.
